elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Rendered text reads "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY ... EXCEED", replacing the one-sided "TRUELINK'S LIABILITY"; the carve-out is likewise party-neutral ("A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS OR ITS BREACH ...").

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The cap remains "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" — no USD 1,000,000 alternative floor, "paid" only (not "paid or payable"), and the 12 months run from an unstated point rather than the event giving rise to the claim.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: No exclusion of indirect, incidental or consequential damages appears in the rendered sentence or elsewhere in the cited language; the drafter concedes in the rationale that this element was not pressed.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Parenthetical carve-out: "(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S ... BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ...)" sits outside the cap and applies to either party.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The carve-out list is limited to indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; data protection and security obligations are not named and therefore remain inside the cap.
"(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ...)" places both parties' indemnities outside the cap.
Carve-out expressly retains "GROSS NEGLIGENCE", now on a mutual basis ("A PARTY'S ... ITS ... GROSS NEGLIGENCE") rather than TrueLink's only.
Carve-out expressly retains "WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" for either party.
Fraud does not appear in the carve-out parenthetical; add "FRAUD" to the excluded matters.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out in the rendered sentence; infringement claims other than those routed through an indemnity remain subject to the cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: No statement that Client's obligation to pay amounts due is not "damages" for cap purposes; as drafted the mutual cap on "ANY MATTER ARISING UNDER OR RELATED TO THIS AGREEMENT" could be read to cap Client's payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "EITHER PARTY'S AGGREGATE LIABILITY" replaces the Vendor-only formulation, and the deterministic check confirms no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Retained basis "THE TOTAL COMPENSATION PAID FOR HOSTING AND SUPPORT SERVICES OVER THE IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING 12 MONTHS PERIOD" is a 12-month fee-based cap; hosting and support compensation is the operative consideration under this hosting/support agreement.

"(OTHER THAN A PARTY'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS ...)" — indemnities of both parties sit outside the cap, curing the walk-away risk of Client's Section 12a indemnity being the only unlimited exposure.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "... OR ITS BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS ..." is an express mutual carve-out.
"GROSS NEGLIGENCE" retained in the carve-out and extended to either party.
"WILLFUL MISCONDUCT" retained in the carve-out and extended to either party.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: mutuality, a 12-month fee-based cap, and carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct are all in the operative sentence, not merely promised in the comment.

Preferred is not complete. To reach it the drafter must (i) add the alternative floor and correct basis — "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000"; (ii) insert a mutual exclusion of indirect, incidental and consequential damages (currently absent from the document entirely); (iii) add "data protection and security obligations", "fraud" and "infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights" to the carve-out list; and (iv) add a sentence that Client's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement is not subject to the cap.

Minimality holds: the edit stays within the single existing sentence, changes only the capped party, the cap's scope and the carve-out list, and retains the existing 12-month compensation basis rather than importing the model formula. Deleting the "SECTION 3, 4, 7 AND 11" scope limiter is within the chosen mutuality/aggregate-cap element — an "aggregate" mutual cap cannot coherently be confined to four Vendor-side sections once Client is brought inside it — and no survival tails, procedures, expense language or extra damages categories were added.

Intent is preserved: no defined term is left dangling (the deleted section list was the only cross-reference and its removal creates no orphan), the Section 12a indemnity survives intact and is expressly outside the cap, and the all-caps drafting convention and remedy structure are unchanged.

Caveat to raise in negotiation rather than a defect: the cap base is "compensation paid for hosting and support services", which is narrower than all fees payable under the Agreement and uses "paid" rather than "paid or payable"; if material amounts are billed outside hosting and support, press the greater-of USD 1,000,000 formulation to avoid an eroded Vendor cap.
